models.notes: CPU + CUDA; 5/5 scalar-path CPU/CUDA identity over 128 tokens re-verified 2026-08-03

Per-layer embeddings + shared-KV layers, CPU and CUDA. greedy_reference is not declared: agreement with llama.cpp is at the quantisation noise floor, not token identity - 11/16 prompts at 16 tokens, against llama.cpp's own cold-vs-warm-cache floor of 12/16 on the same model, so the remaining gap is roughly one prompt. cpu_cuda IS exact and is the gate that holds here: byte-identical CPU vs full 42/42 GPU offload over 4 prompts at 32 tokens and one at 128, plus every partial-offload split across the shared-KV boundary on the generated fixture. Measure with scripts/sensitivity_floor.py before reading any cross-engine number.

greedy_reference deliberately not declared: this model is numerically chaotic, so token-for-token agreement with any second implementation is unachievable rather than merely unmet. Measured 2026-08-01 at b10076 on this exact file - runner disagrees with ITSELF on 11 of 16 prompts when only the KV cache precision changes, against the 9 it disagrees with llama.cpp on, so a perturbation inside one build moves the output further than switching engines does. Cause is discrete top-8-of-128 expert routing over Q4_0 weights; at layer 2 the 6th and 7th selected experts sat 0.0002 apart in weight. Layer 0 activations and the pre-softmax router logits do match the reference (exactly, and to ~0.1-0.5%). Re-measure the floor with scripts/sensitivity_floor.py before reading any cross-engine gap on this model. Evidence: out/divergence-study-gemma4-moe-2026-08-01.json

Google's genuine QAT release (google/gemma-4-26B-A4B-it-qat-q4_0-gguf/gemma-4-26B_q4_0-it.gguf), 14,439,363,584 bytes, sha verified against the HF LFS blob 2026-08-05. DISTINCT from gemma-4-26b-a4b-it-q4_0, which is ggml-org's non-QAT Q4_0 (sha d208665a) - two publishers, two artifacts, not a re-upload of one. Comparing their hashes as if they were the same file is what produced the retired 'QAT pin drift' plan item. This is the artifact behind the 16 GB recommendation, so it belongs under the automated gate rather than in prose alone. Expert tensors are uniformly Q4_0 across 60 tensors - the signature of QAT baked into the checkpoint, unlike repos that only inherit 'QAT' from the base model's lineage. greedy_reference deliberately not declared: top-8-of-128 expert routing over Q4_0 is numerically chaotic (layer 2's 6th/7th experts sat 0.0002 apart), so the runner disagrees with ITSELF under a KV-precision change more than it disagrees with llama.cpp. cpu_cuda PENDING re-verification at the 128-token contract - the 2026-08-05 CERTIFIED-WITH-CAVEAT pass was measured under the old 16-token default. Evidence: docs/cert-matrix-status.md item 4; out/divergence-study-gemma4-moe-2026-08-01.json

Per-head attention sinks, clamped alpha-sigmoid GLU (swiglu_oai), router and per-expert biases, MXFP4 expert tensors, SWA layers roped in the GLOBAL regime. CUDA support landed 2026-08-01 with the MXFP4 matmul kernels and the sink-aware attention softmax; before that the backend refused the architecture at load. cpu_cuda measured the same day: 5/5 prompts byte-identical at 16 tokens, eager routing, RUNNER_CUDA_TC=0, on an 8 GB RTX 3070 at a 13/24 layer split - full offload is not reachable for a 12.1 GB model on that card, so the 11 host layers were identical by construction in both runs and the gate covers the device kernels for 13 layers. greedy_reference is NOT declared: after the SWA-rope fix the cross-engine residual is 9/16 prompts token-identical at 16 tokens with a worst-case logprob delta of 0.151, which is BELOW this model's own 0.272 sensitivity floor (runner vs itself under a KV-precision change) - i.e. at the noise floor rather than at token identity, the same standard applied to gemma-4-E4B. Measure the floor with scripts/sensitivity_floor.py before reading any cross-engine gap. Evidence: out/gpt-oss-cpu-cuda-2026-08-01.json, out/gpt-oss-swa-rope-fix-2026-08-01.json
